## SECTION 12 — VALUATION, EXPECTATIONS GAP & FINAL EXECUTION OPINION

### 12.1 Cash-Flow Definition and Forecasting Method

**Cash-flow definition — Owner FCF:**

The framework's data-pack instruction is explicit: stock-based compensation (SBC) is a real expense that cash-flow statements add back; an owner-earnings figure that does not subtract it is overstated. I therefore define:

**Owner FCF = Operating Cash Flow − Capital Expenditure − SBC**

This is the cash available to shareholders after both physical investment and the cost of maintaining/compensating the workforce through equity. It is conservative in the right way: the company currently spends ~$117M/yr in SBC and simultaneously repurchases stock to counter dilution, so this double effect is already captured in OCF and the share-count decline.

**Why not Net Income:** NI includes non-cash D&A and SBC; OCF embeds working-capital changes and non-cash items. OCF is the closest filed line to true cash generation.

**Why not "cash FCF" only (OCF − capex):** That version treats every SBC share issued as free. The company had to spend $275M on buybacks in H1 2026 to reduce shares; those buybacks are the cash consequence of a heavily equity-compensated payroll. I present the no-SBC version as a cross-check in 12.6.
